title: Days Supply Limits and the 90-Day Maintenance Requirement Across Prescription Insurance on File Plan Classes
content:
Each plan class of **Prescription Insurance on File** caps the days supply one claim may bill, and some classes require maintenance drugs to move to a 90-day supply once a set number of short fills has been paid.

| Plan class | Largest days supply per claim | 90-day maintenance requirement | Courtesy fills of 34 days or less per prescription per plan year |
|---|---|---|---|
| Medicaid Managed Care Pharmacy Benefit | 34 | No | 0 |
| Medicare Part D Standard Plan | 90 | No | 0 |
| Medicare Part D Enhanced Plan | 90 | No | 0 |
| Medicare Advantage Prescription Drug Plan | 90 | No | 0 |
| Commercial High-Deductible Health Plan | 90 | Yes | 2 |
| Commercial Copay Plan | 90 | Yes | 2 |
| Workers' Compensation Pharmacy Benefit | 30 | No | 0 |

## Definitions

- **Largest days supply per claim** — the largest days supply one claim may bill, in days.
- **90-day maintenance requirement** — whether maintenance drugs must move to a 90-day supply after the courtesy fills.
- **Courtesy fills** — paid fills of 34 days or less allowed per prescription per plan year before the 90-day requirement applies.

## Points of reading

- The 90-day requirement and its 2 courtesy fills exist only under the two commercial classes; every other class shows No and 0.
- The shortest caps are the Workers' Compensation Pharmacy Benefit at 30 days and the Medicaid Managed Care Pharmacy Benefit at 34 days; every other class caps a claim at 90 days.
